newsitem.title: EGYPT: Repsol south Egypt oil find seen good omen.
newsitem.headline: Repsol south Egypt oil find seen good omen.

text.p: Spanish oil company Repsol has found traces, or shows, of oil at the first well it has drilled in the Kom Ombo area in the south of Egypt, Egyptian oil industry sources said on Wednesday.
The well is the most southerly in Egypt ever to give shows and could revolutionise the way petroleum geologists look at the south of the country, which they have largely neglected.
"They have good oil shows at Kom Ombo. This could be the turning-point for the whole of Upper Egypt," one source said.
"It shows that there is enough sedimentary basin in the south (for oil to be present)," he added.
Officials at Respol Exploracion Egipto's office in Cairo referred enquiries to their headquarters in Spain.

Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi was quoted in government newspapers on Wednesday as saying the ministry's laboratories would announce within hours the results of the drilling west of Kom Ombo, which lies 650 km (400 miles) south of Cairo.
But his office later said no announcement was imminent. "There are traces but we only make announcements when oil is discovered," a ministry official told Reuters.
The industry sources said the shows at Kom Ombo reinforced the optimism about the south created by discoveries in the Apache Corp concession at Qarun southwest of Cairo.
